---
title: "What to do if I can only print A4?"
---

{{< include _model.qmd >}}

The same parts, re-nested onto A4 instead of tiled across it, and written out as
a two-page 1:1 PDF. The foam is unchanged — it is still the A3 sheet the brief
specifies. Only the paper changes.

::: {.callout-tip}
## Specified
**Re-nest onto A4 rather than tile the A3 across two sheets** · decided here,
2026-08-30 · two A4 portrait sheets side by side come to exactly A3, so tiling
works in principle, but every printer refuses to print to the paper edge and the
seam falls across parts. Re-nesting costs nothing because the only part too big
for A4 is the wing, which the build already splits at the centreline.
:::

```{python}
A4P, A4L = (210.0, 297.0), (297.0, 210.0)    # mm, portrait and landscape
SPLIT_A, SPLIT_B = 0.2665, 0.1800            # m, as the A3 plan

whole_wing = sym_surface(wing_eta, wing_c, b_w / 2)
half = whole_wing[whole_wing[:, 0] <= 0]     # one panel, cut at the centreline
mirrored = half * [-1, 1]

# Splitting a polygon by a coordinate is the kind of thing that silently drops a
# vertex, so the two panels are checked to reconstitute the wing before either
# reaches a printer.
shoelace = lambda q: abs(np.sum(q[:, 0] * np.roll(q[:, 1], -1)
                                - np.roll(q[:, 0], -1) * q[:, 1])) / 2 / 1e6
assert abs(shoelace(half) + shoelace(mirrored) - S_w) < 1e-9, "panels lost area"

sheet1 = nest({
    "wing, left panel": half, "wing, right panel": mirrored,
    "stabilizer": sym_surface(stab_eta, stab_c, b_h / 2), "fin": fin_outline(),
}, {"wing, left panel": (8, 8), "wing, right panel": (8, 112),
    "stabilizer": (8, 218), "fin": (160, 218)}, A4P)

sheet2 = nest({
    "fuselage A, nose": fuselage_outline(0, SPLIT_A),
    "fuselage B, tail": fuselage_outline(SPLIT_B, l_fus),
    "fuselage B, nose": fuselage_outline(0, SPLIT_B),
    "fuselage A, tail": fuselage_outline(SPLIT_A, l_fus),
}, {"fuselage A, nose": (8, 8), "fuselage B, tail": (8, 54),
    "fuselage B, nose": (8, 92), "fuselage A, tail": (8, 138)}, A4L)

short_by = b_w * 1e3 - A4P[1]
PDF = "chapters/02-mceagle-300/mceagle-300-cutting-plan-a4.pdf"
```

**Answer.** Print two A4 sheets — one portrait, one landscape — and cut nothing
across a seam. Every part fits a single sheet except the wing, which at
`{python} f"{b_w*1e3:.0f}"` mm misses A4's `{python} f"{A4P[1]:.0f}"` mm edge by
`{python} f"{short_by:.0f}"` mm. That costs nothing, because the wing is divided
at its centreline during assembly anyway: each panel is
`{python} f"{b_w/2*1e3:.0f}"` × `{python} f"{wing_c[0]*1e3:.1f}"` mm and fits
easily.

Two A4 portrait sheets butted together are exactly A3, so the A3 plan *could* be
tiled instead. It is a worse answer. Printers leave an unprintable margin of
several millimetres, so the join loses material precisely where the wing and the
long fuselage pieces cross it, and those are the parts whose length matters
most. Re-nesting has no seam at all.

Cut the two wing panels as a matched pair — stack the foam and cut both at once
— since they no longer come from one piece split down the middle.

[**Download the 1:1 A4 cutting plan (2 pages)**](mceagle-300-cutting-plan-a4.pdf) —
print at 100%, and check a wing panel measures `{python} f"{b_w/2*1e3:.0f}"` mm
along its straight edge before cutting. Everything else — stations, dihedral,
ballast — is unchanged from the A3 plan.

```{python}
#| label: fig-a4
#| fig-cap: "The same seven pieces on two A4 sheets: wing panels, stabilizer and fin on one; the four fuselage laminations on the other. No part crosses a sheet boundary."
from matplotlib.backends.backend_pdf import PdfPages


def draw(ax, placed, sheet, label=True):
    for n, p in placed.items():
        ax.fill(p[:, 0], p[:, 1], facecolor="none", edgecolor="k", lw=0.6)
        if label:
            ax.text(p[:, 0].mean(), p[:, 1].mean(), n, ha="center", va="center",
                    fontsize=6, color="0.45")
    ax.set_xlim(0, sheet[0]); ax.set_ylim(0, sheet[1])
    ax.set_aspect("equal"); ax.axis("off")


with PdfPages(PDF) as pdf:                       # 1:1 -- one unit per millimetre
    for placed, sheet in [(sheet1, A4P), (sheet2, A4L)]:
        f = plt.figure(figsize=(sheet[0] / 25.4, sheet[1] / 25.4))
        draw(f.add_axes([0, 0, 1, 1]), placed, sheet, label=False)
        pdf.savefig(f); plt.close(f)

fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(9, 4.2))
for ax, (placed, sheet, t) in zip(axes, [(sheet1, A4P, "sheet 1, portrait"),
                                         (sheet2, A4L, "sheet 2, landscape")]):
    draw(ax, placed, sheet)
    ax.add_patch(plt.Rectangle((0, 0), *sheet, fill=False, ec="0.6", lw=1))
    ax.set_title(f"{t} — {sheet[0]:.0f} × {sheet[1]:.0f} mm", fontsize=9)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```
